conductor_note: Boards change between runs — judge fetch counts against the source-reported total, never against last week's number alone; and a Monday run will read thinner than a midweek one, which is calendar, not signal.

data_sources.name: Greenhouse public boards API
data_sources.quality_gate: Every record carries title, URL, date, location, department; duplicates collapsed on source + native ID; field positions asserted per board so a layout change fails loudly instead of writing blank titles.
data_sources.record_type: One job posting (title, URL, date, location, department, ad text) from a Greenhouse-hosted company board.
data_sources.update_freq: Weekly; the 2026-09-26 run fetched the majority of 3,446 postings across 18 boards.

data_sources.name: Ashby posting API
data_sources.quality_gate: Same record standard as Greenhouse; raw responses saved untouched and dated.
data_sources.record_type: One job posting from an Ashby-hosted board (AI labs: OpenAI, Anthropic, Writer, Notion, and others).
data_sources.update_freq: Weekly, same run cadence as Greenhouse.

data_sources.name: SmartRecruiters postings API
data_sources.quality_gate: Same record standard; the paging loop is verified to emit no duplicates across pages. NOTE: only 10 verified records in the 2026-09-26 run — below the 25-record bar; see recipe TODO: DATA SOURCE.
data_sources.record_type: One job posting from a SmartRecruiters-hosted board (Canva); paged 100 at a time with one extra call per posting for the description.

one_thing: Lectern is the only job-board reader that turns listings into checkable evidence of a company's interest in teaching, for the independent education consultant, without asking them to pretend to be a job seeker.

phase_gates.bad_looks_like: A whole ATS returns nothing, or a board that had 248 postings returns 12.
phase_gates.good_looks_like: Every source returned its expected board count; raw responses saved untouched, dated, per source; fetch counts recorded next to the source-reported totals. (A Figma fetch of 151 against a 160-posting snapshot is expected drift; a fetch of 12 is not.)
phase_gates.response: Log and continue — the failure is recorded as unavailable and the other sources keep going. Flag for review if an entire ATS is dark across two runs.

phase_gates.bad_looks_like: Field assertions raise (the board changed its layout), or a run lands under 90% of the reported total.
phase_gates.good_looks_like: 100% of records carry title, URL, date, location, department; duplicates collapsed on source + native ID (0 remaining); field assertions passed. A run is trusted only at >=90% of the source-reported total and >=70% of the previous trusted run.
phase_gates.response: Hard stop for that source's downstream — nothing blank is ever written, and an untrusted run freezes the closed-job logic (it may update 'seen' timestamps, but it closes nothing).

phase_gates.bad_looks_like: A rule keeps postings at ~1-in-10 precision (as the first teaching-materials rule did), or a demand claim appears with no raw link behind it.
phase_gates.good_looks_like: Every kept posting names the rule that fired and the words that matched; every rejected posting names its reason; the demand ranking links each company claim to its signal roles; the new/gone diff compares native IDs across two trusted runs. Trust test: pick any claim at random — you can reach the raw posting in two clicks.
phase_gates.response: Flag for review, then fix and re-audit. An unlinked claim is a bug, not a judgment call: hard stop until it is traced or removed.

phase_gates.bad_looks_like: Numbers that cannot be recomputed from committed files, or limits hidden — an unreadable company presented as 'no demand.' (Derived from Part 4's good-looks-like; Part 5 defines no Step 4 failure mode.)
phase_gates.good_looks_like: A non-technical reader can answer 'which companies, what roles, what's new this month' from page one; every number is recomputable from the committed files; the report states its limits (unreadable companies, unverified totals) instead of hiding them.
phase_gates.response: Flag for review — a human reads the report before it ships.

primary_user.role: Independent AI-education consultant — typically a working professor or former educator selling teaching expertise to software vendors.
primary_user.situation: They want an education-advocate role (flexible, part-time, or consulting) with a company whose tools they already teach. That role is almost never posted, so the real job is figuring out which companies are worth approaching, and when.
primary_user.workaround: Scrolling careers pages by hand (an hour a week, first thing to get skipped), LinkedIn job alerts on titles like 'advocate,' and conference chatter.

tool_summary: Lectern helps an independent AI-education consultant find which companies selling AI to universities are showing real interest in how their tools are used in teaching, so they can pitch a role that hasn't been posted yet.
